newsitem.title: GERMANY: SGL Carbon ups 96 profit, reveals takeovers.
newsitem.headline: SGL Carbon ups 96 profit, reveals takeovers.

text.p: German SGL Carbon AG on Friday said it posted stronger 1996 profits and moved one step closer to acquiring larger market shares by acquiring two more groups.

SGL Carbon, the world's largest carbon and graphite maker producing a range of products for the electrical, steel and semiconductor industries, said provisional 1996 group operating profit climbed 25 percent to 324 million marks.
Group sales rose by 13 percent to 1.74 billion marks.
The group was silent on its dividend plans, saying a decision would be announced after the group's supervisory board meeting on February 28.

But analysts generally expect an increase from 1995's 1.67 mark-payout after management board chairman Robert Koehler promised a higher dividend only two months ago when he forecast the group's annual profit would top 300 million marks.
To expand in the U.S. market, home of SGL Carbon's biggest competitors, SGL Carbon acquired privately-held specialty graphite group M.G.P. Inc located in Topton, Pennsylvania.
M.G.P. posted sales of $11 million last year.

"This acquisition underscores our plans to concentrate our specialty graphite business where our customers are which allows us to optimise our service-oriented business," SGL Carbon said in a statement.

SGL Carbon also said it had strengthened its electrical contacts business by purchasing some businesses from Berliner Elektrokohle Lichtenberg AG. These businesses will increase group sales by about 12 million marks, SGL Carbon said.
SGL Carbon said it saw synergies having a positive impact on results even though one-off costs related to the sale would need to be digested this year.
